title: [WT-18] Docs: worktree mode in the narrative guides and the worker role docs
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §0, §2, §3, §6 and §7.6.

Objective: agents and humans reading the guides learn the worktree delivery path, and the worker role doc stops telling workers never to use .worktrees/. This is the other half of the docs sweep, split from WT-17 for the 5-file cap.

Deliverable:
- Root CLAUDE.md, 'Working in this repo' and Landing: the worktree mode summary (per-task W on moe/task/<id>, landing to main by merge-tree + CAS, board history on refs/moe/board, control checkout on moe/control) and the settings key list.
- scripts/CLAUDE.md, 'Land on every exit': a worktree-mode arm covering L0-L14, the unlanded route, DENY in W, the control-seat no-op, removal and sweep. Keep the shared-mode text intact.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Delivery Path': the worktree variant; the daemon stays state-only.
- docs/roles/worker.md line 13 ('work in the project root ... never a .worktrees/ checkout') becomes mode-aware: in worktree mode the wrapper has already put you in your task worktree. Keep the role doc within the 40-line lint cap.
- docs/roles/worker.reference.md: the using-git-worktrees row and the attribution paragraph gain the worktree-mode behaviour.
- A VS Code note (no code change) goes in CLAUDE.md's package table row.
Read the landed code for spellings.

NOT in scope: MCP_SERVER, SCHEMA and CONFIGURATION (WT-17); TROUBLESHOOTING (WT-16); code; .moe/roles copies (the plugins sync them).

Verification: npm run lint && grep -q 'moe/task/' CLAUDE.md && grep -q 'worktree' scripts/CLAUDE.md && grep -qi 'worktree' docs/ARCHITECTURE.md && grep -qi 'worktree mode' docs/roles/worker.md

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/CLAUDE.md: add ONE new top-level bullet, `- **Land on every exit, worktree mode** (...)`.

PLACEMENT AND STYLE
- It is the next top-level bullet after the existing `- **Land on every exit**` bullet: insert it after that bullet's `  **Agent Git-write guard:**` continuation line (:12) and before `- **Heartbeat sidecar**`.
- Change no existing byte of the file. Step 5 compares the shared Land bullet and its guard line with your task's base (DoD 2).
- Follow the file's style: one lead line, then 2-space-indented `  - ` sub-bullets, short sentences, codes in backticks.

COVER, as the landed code does it (step-1 inventory), each item with its codes:
1. Scope.
   - The mode is pinned per attempt. A worker takes it from the claim's `workspace`, else from a pre-flight get_context that answered for this task.
   - A control seat (architect, QA, governor) is in worktree mode only while the control checkout's HEAD is refs/heads/moe/control.
   - Document 31187ec1's MOE_WORKTREE_CONTEXT_FAILED contract as it landed.
2. Provisioning at the worker pre-flight.
   - W = `.worktrees/<taskId>` on `moe/task/<taskId>`: locked, sparse `'/*' '!/.moe/'`, cut from the target's authority, and reused across sessions (re-added on an existing branch).
   - The guard codes each stop the seat with report_blocked, launch no CLI and never fall back to the shared checkout.
   - Every CLI runs in W, including the PowerShell claude launch. MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control checkout; MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET are exported.
   - Per-W configs; the Serena root is W, with shared memory and skills links recorded in the manifest; MOE_WORKTREE_SERENA_OUTSIDE, MOE_WORKTREE_LINK_FAILED, MOE_WORKTREE_DEPS_MISSING.
3. Attribution in W.
   - No baseline and no tiers: every dirty path in W lands except DENY.
   - DENY is `denied_wt`: today's list, `.moe/**` with no BOARD exception, plus `.claude/skills/**` (MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDED).
   - MOE_WORKTREE_STRAY_EDIT: edits in the control checkout are reported, never landed or reverted.
4. Checkpoints. L0-L2 land on the task branch only, pushed per checkpointPush and never forced. A W found dirty at pre-flight gets a recovery checkpoint (MOE_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERED).
5. Completion, L0-L14 with codes:
   - the owner guard;
   - the `git-land-<target>` lease, only while a qualityGate is set;
   - `sync_land_target`: in remote mode B is refs/remotes/origin/<target>; divergence and fetch-failure codes;
   - one `merge-tree` squash of the task's net change onto B, then the board guard;
   - the gate on exactly that merged tree on EVERY completion while a qualityGate is set (qualityGateScope ignored), in a sparse .moe-free gate worktree;
   - hooks, then the receipt journal before anything is published;
   - publication: a CAS update-ref in local mode; in remote mode a non-forced push, which is the only publication, with the local target a mirror;
   - push results: `[rejected]` ends the round, `[remote rejected]` is unlanded `remote`, anything else goes to `reconcile_push`;
   - an unknown outcome moves no ref, keeps the journal and leaves the attempt `finalizing` (rescue reason push-unknown);
   - the round limits; the task-branch sync; record_commit and finalize_attempt; the control follow; the lease released on every path.
   - Target rules: a literal consolidationBranch, else main; MOE_LAND_TARGET_CHECKED_OUT. In worktree mode the peel, the branch-safety check and moe/work-<date> are retired, and MOE_PUSH_REBASE is ignored.
6. The unlanded route, taken only when nothing was published.
   - Its codes, a rescue ref with the reason, and finalize_attempt 'unlanded'.
   - The daemon routes the row back with landingRetry: to WORKING, or to BLOCKED for diverged or a 3rd consecutive failure.
   - The next pre-flight merges the target into W and prompts `LANDING-CONFLICT:` or `LANDING-RETRY:`; then the marker check. Never auto-resolved.
7. Replay settles a journaled completion and never re-lands it.
8. Control seats land nothing (MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT).
9. Board history snapshots go on refs/moe/board; commitBoardState switches them.
10. The control checkout on moe/control fast-forwards after landings, at the loop top before the hot-reload check, and in QA's pre-flight with its ancestry check. Include MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE.
11. Removal and the sweep.
   - Removal at DONE by the QA post-flight (`task_branch_landed`).
   - The orphan sweep: interval, lock, per-pass bound, a worktree-orphan rescue before any delete, links unlinked first.
   - Moe touches only `.worktrees/task-*`; human .worktrees/ checkouts stay theirs.
12. If HEAD has it, the human-run migration landing `--land-branch` / `-LandBranch`, with a link to WT-16's runbook in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md (an anchor that exists).
13. Tests: name only files on HEAD (`git ls-files scripts/tests | grep -iE 'worktree|migration'`).

WHAT STEP 5 CHECKS
- The six strings `moe/task/`, `unlanded`, `LANDING-CONFLICT:`, `LANDING-RETRY:`, `refs/moe/board` and `moe/control`.
- Every code of those families in HEAD's moe-agent.sh, as a whole word. The list grows with whatever WT-11..WT-14 and WT-10M landed.
- `--land-branch`, once HEAD has it.
- Every MOE_ token, Verb-Moe* cmdlet and backticked snake_case helper you write must exist in HEAD's wrappers. Write MCP tools as `moe.<name>` or without backticks.
- daemonGitDocs.test.ts fails on 'never runs/executes/touches git', 'runs no git' and 'does not run git' in any doc line. Say the daemon never writes git state instead.

ERROR HANDLING. Describe the error handling of each failure path as the code implements it: its code, whether it stops or routes, what moves and what never moves. Never paraphrase a refusal into a fallback. Keep every negative: never forced, no local-CAS fallback in remote mode, never auto-resolved, replay never re-lands, no unlanded commit deleted without a rescue ref.

implementationPlan.description:
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, `## Delivery Path`: add a `### Worktree mode` subsection.

PLACEMENT
- Put it AFTER the record-directories list, whose last bullet is `- \`receipts/\`: …` (:283-285), and immediately BEFORE `### The verified-local path` (:287).
- Not earlier: a ### heading above 'The five record directories' would pull the shared-mode paragraphs into the subsection. Step 5 enforces the position.
- Wrap at the file's ~80 columns; about 20-35 lines.

CONTENT. Take spellings from the step-1 inventory and from WT-17a's MCP_SERVER/SCHEMA text.
1. The setting and the pin.
   - `settings.worktreeMode`: 'off' by default; `resolveWorktreeMode`.
   - claim_next_task pins `workspaceMode` on the attempt. Both claim_next_task and get_context expose `workspace: { mode, path, branch, target }`.
   - Only a WORKING claim gets 'worktree'. complete_task then expects branch `moe/task/<taskId>`.
2. A worker's bytes live in its task worktree on `moe/task/<taskId>`, a sparse checkout with no `.moe/`. Checkpoints land only on that branch.
3. How end-to-end steps 3-4 change. A completion lands as ONE squash commit on the target (a literal consolidationBranch, else main):
   - `merge-tree` of the target tip and the task branch;
   - the gate on exactly that merged tree, on every completion while a qualityGate is set (qualityGateScope ignored), in a .moe-free gate worktree;
   - the receipt journal before any publication, on every completion (a gate-less one has no Candidate);
   - then publication: a CAS update-ref in local mode, or in remote mode a non-forced push, which is the only publication (the local target is a mirror).
   An unknown push outcome keeps the attempt `finalizing` until a fetch settles it.
4. A landing that publishes nothing (a conflict, a gate failure, a diverged or failed fetch, a refused push, exhausted rounds) closes the attempt `unlanded` with a rescue ref.
   - The daemon routes the row back to WORKING, or to BLOCKED for `diverged` or a 3rd consecutive failure, with `Task.landingRetry`.
   - The next `landed` finalize clears landingRetry. The next worker resolves the failure in its worktree.
5. Board history goes to `refs/moe/board`. The tracked `.moe/tasks` records stay frozen on the target from the switch on.
6. The control checkout sits on `moe/control` and fast-forwards to the target. QA reviews only landed commits.
7. Close with the invariant. Worktree mode adds daemon state (`workspaceMode`, `workspace`, `landingRetry`, the `unlanded` outcome) but no daemon git write: every git write is still the wrapper's. Shared mode is unchanged.

KEEP UNCHANGED
- `**The daemon is state-only.**` and every existing Delivery Path line.
- The one permitted exception: the intro paragraph's gate sentence (the one ending '`MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE` is not `1`') may gain '(shared mode; see **Worktree mode** below)'.
- Do not reword 'The daemon never runs claude and never opens a file inside a Claude config folder' (account-trust-docs.test.mjs).
- Do not reword the `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch` / util/cachedPlanPaths.ts / 'without claiming remote freshness' text (daemonGitDocs.test.ts).
- Never use the phrases daemonGitDocs.test.ts forbids (see step 2).

ERROR HANDLING. Describe the error handling of each failure path as published-nothing or finalizing, exactly as the code does it.

Your step 1 greps the MOE_WORKTREE_* codes, so it will pick the code up if 31187ec1 lands first. Document its contract in scripts/CLAUDE.md's worktree arm:
- A worker's mode comes from the claim's workspace, else from a get_context that answered for this task. On that reply, an absent workspace still means shared.
